Subject: Fairview — incident update and immediate next steps (post-mitigation)

Team / Priya — closing the active bridge with a summary and next steps for the executive inbox. Thanks to everyone who jumped on the call. Quick incident recap and customer-facing summary below for records.

What happened (tl;dr):
- At ~21:44 UTC a subset of NPU host nodes in the Fairview-serving pool experienced a firmware/driver regression during scheduled maintenance on the partner infra (external vendor patch), causing increased kernel-level queuing and multiple worker restarts. This produced cascading backpressure at the request router and inflated p95 latency and 5xx rates.

Mitigation performed (timeline):
- 22:05 UTC: pinned Fairview traffic to warm fallback model variant (lower max concurrency) which reduced individual request timeouts.
- 22:12 UTC: scaled additional hot nodes and rebalanced traffic away from affected hosts (temporary improvement).
- 22:22 UTC: rolled back canary routing that introduced a quantized variant for a narrow subset — found no evidence that model artifact itself caused failures.
- 22:45 UTC: vendor confirmed a driver rollback on affected NPU hosts; kernel panics stopped and worker restarts stabilized.
- 23:05 UTC: p95 latency returned to ~520ms; error rate fallen to ~0.2% and throughput recovered to ~540 rps.

Customer impact: Fairview experienced ~35 minutes of elevated errors and latency; conversion loss estimated at ~0.8% of daily revenue window (preliminary). We are coordinating final impact calc with finance.

Immediate next steps / commitments:
- (Action) Redwood infra: complete full post-incident tracing export and share with Fairview SRE by 2026-12-12 10:00 UTC (I own).
- (Action) Marcus: run a thorough node-level postmortem focused on driver/kernel interactions and share remediation pull requests (SERV-2149).
- (Action) Marissa: prepare customer compensation options (credit tiers and SLA exceptions) and a concise public statement by 2026-12-12 12:00 UTC.
- (Action) Neha: codify a routing-safety gate to prevent automatic canary routing to quantized variants without a 2x stress validation for the next 90 days.

Customer comms: Marissa will propose the customer-safe statement; Irene to send once approved. We plan an executive note to Fairview leadership with root cause, timeline, and compensation offer.

Attachments: postmortem-mitigation-checklist.pdf (internal), error-sample-20261211.log (from customer), grafana-export-20261211.json (customer).

If anyone needs to reopen the bridge, call it and I will rehost — otherwise we will track follow-ups on SERV-2149 and the customer Jira.
